\section[opinar]{opinar — to think, to have an opinion}

\label{lesson:ES-C493-opinar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to choose, then the Spanish for to keep.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: opinar}
\textbf{opinar} — \textquotedblleft{}to think, to have an opinion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
¿Qué opinas del plan?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{What do you think of the plan?}
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{opinar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{opinar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{opinar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to choose, then the Spanish for to keep, then say \emph{opinar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does opinar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To think, to have an opinion\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[convencer]{convencer — to convince}

\label{lesson:ES-C493-convencer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to keep, then the Spanish for to think.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: convencer}
\textbf{convencer} — \textquotedblleft{}to convince\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No me convence la idea.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I am not convinced by the idea.}
\end{quote}

It takes a \emph{z} in the first person present: \emph{convenzo}.

One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.

\section[sugerir]{sugerir — to suggest}

\section[la duda]{la duda — the doubt; the question}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la duda}
\textbf{la duda} — \textquotedblleft{}the doubt; the question\textquotedblright{}.

(\textbf{toser}.) To breathe? (\textbf{respirar}.) The aspirin? (\textbf{la aspirina}.) The vaccine? (\textbf{la vacuna}.) To be glad? (\textbf{alegrarse}.) To get angry? (\textbf{enfadarse}.) To worry? (\textbf{preocuparse}.) To relax? (\textbf{relajarse}.) To have fun? (\textbf{divertirse}.) To get married? (\textbf{casarse}.) To get divorced? (\textbf{divorciarse}.) To fall in love?
